commit_message:
[Codegen] Add bufferization support for CastToRaggedShapeOp and LinearizeRaggedDimsOp (#24193)

This is PR 4/N of landing block sparse changes that are captured in this
branch :


https://github.com/MaheshRavishankar/iree/tree/users/MaheshRavishankar/blockSparseCommits

Adds `BufferizableOpInterfac`e external models for two tensor-ext ops
that describe ragged shapes:
- `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape` — reinterprets a source buffer
as a rank-(n+1) ragged buffer by
attaching a RaggedShapeAttr as the memref layout.
-`iree_tensor_ext.linearize_ragged_dims` — the inverse view: collapses
the ragged dimensions of a source
buffer back into a single dense dimension and drops the ragged layout.
  
Both ops are pure views, so the interface implementations:
- Report the operands as reads and never as writes (including
`resultBufferizesToMemoryWrite = false`).
- Set `mustBufferizeInPlace = true` and mark the result as
`BufferRelation::Equivalent` to source, so
bufferization does not introduce a copy.
- For `cast_to_ragged_shape`, the result memref's layout is the ragged
encoding promoted from the tensor
encoding; operand buffers use the identity layout.
- For `linearize_ragged_dims`, both operand and result memrefs use the
identity layout; the result simply
drops the ragged encoding.
`bufferize` replaces the tensor-typed op with an identical memref-typed
version of itself — no data is
moved.

commit_message:
[TensorExt] Add ResolveSparseInterfaceOps pass and rewrite patterns

After bufferization, a memref produced by `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape`
carries a ragged layout that the backends cannot lower directly. This adds
patterns that rewrite reads from such memrefs into reads from the underlying
source memref, using `SparseOpInterface::resolveRange` to translate the ragged
(row, column) indices into linearized source indices.

Patterns (`populateSparseInterfaceRewritePatterns`):
- `vector.transfer_read`, `vector.load`, `vector.maskedload` and `memref.load`
  from a ragged-shaped memref are rewritten to read from the source. For
  `vector.transfer_read` the permutation map and `in_bounds` are remapped to
  the collapsed source dimensions; reads whose vector dims touch the sparse
  dims are left alone.

Patterns (`populateResolveDimOfCastToRaggedShapePatterns`):
- `tensor.dim`/`memref.dim` of the ragged-row dimension of a
  `cast_to_ragged_shape` result folds to `numRaggedRows`. The ragged column
  dimension varies per row and is not resolved.

The `iree-tensor-ext-resolve-sparse-interface-ops` pass applies the first set
with the greedy driver. Region simplification is disabled in its config: the
pass only rewrites memory accesses and must not merge blocks or otherwise
restructure control flow (the default `Aggressive` level does so even when no
pattern applies, which broke later lowering on CPU).

The patterns are tested through the existing
`iree-tensor-ext-test-sparse-op-interface-methods` pass via a new
`test-resolve-range-rewriters` option. The pass is not added to any pipeline
yet; that happens in a follow-up.

commit_message:
[TensorExt] Add ResolveSparseInterfaceOps pass and rewrite patterns

After bufferization, a memref produced by `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape`
carries a ragged layout that the backends cannot lower directly. This adds
patterns that rewrite reads from such memrefs into reads from the underlying
source memref, using `SparseOpInterface::resolveRange` to translate the ragged
(row, column) indices into linearized source indices.

Patterns (`populateSparseInterfaceRewritePatterns`):
- `vector.transfer_read`, `vector.load`, `vector.maskedload` and `memref.load`
  from a ragged-shaped memref are rewritten to read from the source. For
  `vector.transfer_read` the permutation map and `in_bounds` are remapped to
  the collapsed source dimensions; reads whose vector dims touch the sparse
  dims are left alone.

Patterns (`populateResolveDimOfCastToRaggedShapePatterns`):
- `tensor.dim`/`memref.dim` of the ragged-row dimension of a
  `cast_to_ragged_shape` result folds to `numRaggedRows`. The ragged column
  dimension varies per row and is not resolved.

The `iree-tensor-ext-resolve-sparse-interface-ops` pass applies the first set
with the greedy driver. Region simplification is disabled in its config: the
pass only rewrites memory accesses and must not merge blocks or otherwise
restructure control flow (the default `Aggressive` level does so even when no
pattern applies, which broke later lowering on CPU).

The patterns are tested through the existing
`iree-tensor-ext-test-sparse-op-interface-methods` pass via a new
`test-resolve-range-rewriters` option. The pass is not added to any pipeline
yet; that happens in a follow-up.

commit_message:
[TensorExt] Add ResolveSparseInterfaceOps pass and rewrite patterns

After bufferization, a memref produced by `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape`
carries a ragged layout that the backends cannot lower directly. This adds
patterns that rewrite reads from such memrefs into reads from the underlying
source memref, using `SparseOpInterface::resolveRange` to translate the ragged
(row, column) indices into linearized source indices.

Patterns (`populateSparseInterfaceRewritePatterns`):
- `vector.transfer_read`, `vector.load`, `vector.maskedload` and `memref.load`
  from a ragged-shaped memref are rewritten to read from the source. For
  `vector.transfer_read` the permutation map and `in_bounds` are remapped to
  the collapsed source dimensions; reads whose vector dims touch the sparse
  dims are left alone.

Patterns (`populateResolveDimOfCastToRaggedShapePatterns`):
- `tensor.dim`/`memref.dim` of the ragged-row dimension of a
  `cast_to_ragged_shape` result folds to `numRaggedRows`. The ragged column
  dimension varies per row and is not resolved.

The `iree-tensor-ext-resolve-sparse-interface-ops` pass applies the first set
with the greedy driver. Region simplification is disabled in its config: the
pass only rewrites memory accesses and must not merge blocks or otherwise
restructure control flow (the default `Aggressive` level does so even when no
pattern applies, which broke later lowering on CPU).

The patterns are tested through the existing
`iree-tensor-ext-test-sparse-op-interface-methods` pass via a new
`test-resolve-range-rewriters` option. The pass is not added to any pipeline
yet; that happens in a follow-up.

After bufferization, a memref produced by `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape`
carries a ragged layout that the backends cannot lower directly. This adds
patterns that rewrite reads from such memrefs into reads from the underlying
source memref, using `SparseOpInterface::resolveRange` to translate the ragged
(row, column) indices into linearized source indices.

Patterns (`populateSparseInterfaceRewritePatterns`):
- `vector.transfer_read`, `vector.load`, `vector.maskedload` and `memref.load`
  from a ragged-shaped memref are rewritten to read from the source. For
  `vector.transfer_read` the permutation map and `in_bounds` are remapped to
  the collapsed source dimensions; reads whose vector dims touch the sparse
  dims are left alone.

  dimension varies per row and is not resolved.

commit_message:
[TensorExt] Add ResolveSparseInterfaceOps pass and rewrite patterns

After bufferization, a memref produced by `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape`
carries a ragged layout that the backends cannot lower directly. This adds
patterns that rewrite reads from such memrefs into reads from the underlying
source memref, using `SparseOpInterface::resolveRange` to translate the ragged
(row, column) indices into linearized source indices.

Patterns (`populateSparseInterfaceRewritePatterns`):
- `vector.transfer_read`, `vector.load`, `vector.maskedload` and `memref.load`
  from a ragged-shaped memref are rewritten to read from the source. For
  `vector.transfer_read` the permutation map and `in_bounds` are remapped to
  the collapsed source dimensions; reads whose vector dims touch the sparse
  dims are left alone.

Patterns (`populateResolveDimOfCastToRaggedShapePatterns`):
- `tensor.dim`/`memref.dim` of the ragged-row dimension of a
  `cast_to_ragged_shape` result folds to `numRaggedRows`. The ragged column
  dimension varies per row and is not resolved.

The `iree-tensor-ext-resolve-sparse-interface-ops` pass applies the first set
with the greedy driver. Region simplification is disabled in its config: the
pass only rewrites memory accesses and must not merge blocks or otherwise
restructure control flow (the default `Aggressive` level does so even when no
pattern applies, which broke later lowering on CPU).

The patterns are tested through the existing
`iree-tensor-ext-test-sparse-op-interface-methods` pass via a new
`test-resolve-range-rewriters` option. The pass is not added to any pipeline
yet; that happens in a follow-up.

commit_message:
[TensorExt] Add ResolveSparseInterfaceOps pass and rewrite patterns

After bufferization, a memref produced by `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape`
carries a ragged layout that the backends cannot lower directly. This adds
patterns that rewrite reads from such memrefs into reads from the underlying
source memref, using `SparseOpInterface::resolveRange` to translate the ragged
(row, column) indices into linearized source indices.

Patterns (`populateSparseInterfaceRewritePatterns`):
- `vector.transfer_read`, `vector.load`, `vector.maskedload` and `memref.load`
  from a ragged-shaped memref are rewritten to read from the source. For
  `vector.transfer_read` the permutation map and `in_bounds` are remapped to
  the collapsed source dimensions; reads whose vector dims touch the sparse
  dims are left alone.

Patterns (`populateResolveDimOfCastToRaggedShapePatterns`):
- `tensor.dim`/`memref.dim` of the ragged-row dimension of a
  `cast_to_ragged_shape` result folds to `numRaggedRows`. The ragged column
  dimension varies per row and is not resolved.

The `iree-tensor-ext-resolve-sparse-interface-ops` pass applies the first set
with the greedy driver. Region simplification is disabled in its config: the
pass only rewrites memory accesses and must not merge blocks or otherwise
restructure control flow (the default `Aggressive` level does so even when no
pattern applies, which broke later lowering on CPU).

`iree-tensor-ext-test-sparse-op-interface-methods` pass via a new

commit_message:
[TensorExt] Add ResolveSparseInterfaceOps pass and rewrite patterns

After bufferization, a memref produced by `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape`
carries a ragged layout that the backends cannot lower directly. This adds
patterns that rewrite reads from such memrefs into reads from the underlying
source memref, using `SparseOpInterface::resolveRange` to translate the ragged
(row, column) indices into linearized source indices.

Patterns (`populateSparseInterfaceRewritePatterns`):
- `vector.transfer_read`, `vector.load`, `vector.maskedload` and `memref.load`
  from a ragged-shaped memref are rewritten to read from the source. For
  `vector.transfer_read` the permutation map and `in_bounds` are remapped to
  the collapsed source dimensions; reads whose vector dims touch the sparse
  dims are left alone.

Patterns (`populateResolveDimOfCastToRaggedShapePatterns`):
- `tensor.dim`/`memref.dim` of the ragged-row dimension of a
  `cast_to_ragged_shape` result folds to `numRaggedRows`. The ragged column
  dimension varies per row and is not resolved.

The `iree-tensor-ext-resolve-sparse-interface-ops` pass applies the first set
with the greedy driver. Region simplification is disabled in its config: the
pass only rewrites memory accesses and must not merge blocks or otherwise
restructure control flow (the default `Aggressive` level does so even when no
pattern applies, which broke later lowering on CPU).

The patterns are tested through the existing
`iree-tensor-ext-test-sparse-op-interface-methods` pass via a new
`test-resolve-range-rewriters` option. The pass is not added to any pipeline
yet; that happens in a follow-up.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Add bufferization support for CastToRaggedShapeOp and LinearizeRaggedDimsOp (#24193)

This is PR 4/N of landing block sparse changes that are captured in this
branch :


https://github.com/MaheshRavishankar/iree/tree/users/MaheshRavishankar/blockSparseCommits

Adds `BufferizableOpInterfac`e external models for two tensor-ext ops
that describe ragged shapes:
- `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape` — reinterprets a source buffer
as a rank-(n+1) ragged buffer by
attaching a RaggedShapeAttr as the memref layout.
-`iree_tensor_ext.linearize_ragged_dims` — the inverse view: collapses
the ragged dimensions of a source
buffer back into a single dense dimension and drops the ragged layout.
  
Both ops are pure views, so the interface implementations:
- Report the operands as reads and never as writes (including
`resultBufferizesToMemoryWrite = false`).
- Set `mustBufferizeInPlace = true` and mark the result as
`BufferRelation::Equivalent` to source, so
bufferization does not introduce a copy.
- For `cast_to_ragged_shape`, the result memref's layout is the ragged
encoding promoted from the tensor
encoding; operand buffers use the identity layout.
- For `linearize_ragged_dims`, both operand and result memrefs use the
identity layout; the result simply
drops the ragged encoding.
`bufferize` replaces the tensor-typed op with an identical memref-typed
version of itself — no data is
moved.
name: ci_summary / summary

that describe ragged shapes:

[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 201b80fb (#25046)

Updates torch-mlir from its October 2 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@201b80fb`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/201b80fb46733537ff6f90d2bdd57b5ba34b26a1),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@52f5c1c4`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/52f5c1c4b86cc812227367c7c49c2d3f40b69e57)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261014`) adapted to IREE's current LLVM
revision.

On top of canonical torch-mlir, the integration branch carries the
adaptation patches already on IREE's current pin that upstream does not
have yet: the LLVM submodule bump, `SymbolOpInterface` for
`ClassTypeOp`/`GlobalSlotOp`, and the TMTensor strict-properties
assembly fix.

ONNX op test expectations:

- Now passing, removed from `expected_compile_failures` in the
CI-exercised configs: `quantizelinear_axis`.

- `test_dequantizelinear_uint16` now fails to compile and is marked as
an expected compile failure, since the new `DequantizeLinear` conversion
does not support uint16 yet.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-token quantization to LinalgExt

Convert quantized_decomposed.quantize_per_token and dequantize_per_token
to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and dequantize_affine. As in
torchao's PerToken granularity, the block size is one along every input
dimension but the last, which each block spans, so the parameters are
indexed by the leading dimensions and the data path needs no reshape.
The unit last dimension that PT2E keeps in the parameters is dropped
like any other static unit dimension.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-token quantization to LinalgExt

Convert quantized_decomposed.quantize_per_token and dequantize_per_token
to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and dequantize_affine. As in
torchao's PerToken granularity, the block size is one along every input
dimension but the last, which each block spans, so the parameters are
indexed by the leading dimensions and the data path needs no reshape.
The unit last dimension that PT2E keeps in the parameters is dropped
like any other static unit dimension.

Per-token needs no reshape, so only the checks shared with the other
granularities apply.

Quantization computes in the scale type, f64 for the scales that
torch.ao computes per token, as the per-token reference does.
Dequantization matches the PT2E reference. The per-token reference adds
the zero point before rounding, so quantize ties with odd zero points
differ from it and from the Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which follows it.

Depends on the torch-mlir ops from llvm/torch-mlir#4765.

Convert quantized_decomposed.quantize_per_token and dequantize_per_token
to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and dequantize_affine. As in
torchao's PerToken granularity, the block size is one along every input
dimension but the last, which each block spans, so the parameters are
indexed by the leading dimensions and the data path needs no reshape.
The unit last dimension that PT2E keeps in the parameters is dropped
like any other static unit dimension.

Per-token needs no reshape, so only the checks shared with the other
granularities apply.

Quantization computes in the scale type, f64 for the scales that
torch.ao computes per token, as the per-token reference does.
Dequantization matches the PT2E reference. The per-token reference adds
the zero point before rounding, so quantize ties with odd zero points
differ from it and from the Torch-to-Linalg lowering, which follows it.

Depends on the torch-mlir ops from llvm/torch-mlir#4765.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_ops :: amdgpu_vulkan_rdna3_O0

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 201b80fb (#25046)

Updates torch-mlir from its October 2 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@201b80fb`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/201b80fb46733537ff6f90d2bdd57b5ba34b26a1),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@52f5c1c4`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/52f5c1c4b86cc812227367c7c49c2d3f40b69e57)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261014`) adapted to IREE's current LLVM
revision.

On top of canonical torch-mlir, the integration branch carries the
adaptation patches already on IREE's current pin that upstream does not
have yet: the LLVM submodule bump, `SymbolOpInterface` for
`ClassTypeOp`/`GlobalSlotOp`, and the TMTensor strict-properties
assembly fix.

ONNX op test expectations:

- Now passing, removed from `expected_compile_failures` in the
CI-exercised configs: `quantizelinear_axis`.

- `test_dequantizelinear_uint16` now fails to compile and is marked as
an expected compile failure, since the new `DequantizeLinear` conversion
does not support uint16 yet.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: issue-greeter

commit_message:
[Codegen] Add bufferization support for CastToRaggedShapeOp and LinearizeRaggedDimsOp (#24193)

This is PR 4/N of landing block sparse changes that are captured in this
branch :


https://github.com/MaheshRavishankar/iree/tree/users/MaheshRavishankar/blockSparseCommits

Adds `BufferizableOpInterfac`e external models for two tensor-ext ops
that describe ragged shapes:
- `iree_tensor_ext.cast_to_ragged_shape` — reinterprets a source buffer
as a rank-(n+1) ragged buffer by
attaching a RaggedShapeAttr as the memref layout.
-`iree_tensor_ext.linearize_ragged_dims` — the inverse view: collapses
the ragged dimensions of a source
buffer back into a single dense dimension and drops the ragged layout.
  
Both ops are pure views, so the interface implementations:
- Report the operands as reads and never as writes (including
`resultBufferizesToMemoryWrite = false`).
- Set `mustBufferizeInPlace = true` and mark the result as
`BufferRelation::Equivalent` to source, so
bufferization does not introduce a copy.
- For `cast_to_ragged_shape`, the result memref's layout is the ragged
encoding promoted from the tensor
encoding; operand buffers use the identity layout.
- For `linearize_ragged_dims`, both operand and result memrefs use the
identity layout; the result simply
drops the ragged encoding.
`bufferize` replaces the tensor-typed op with an identical memref-typed
version of itself — no data is
moved.

commit_message:
Add big-endian MIPS64 (mips64) VMVX-only runtime cross-compilation

Extends the little-endian MIPS64 (mips64el) VMVX runtime to big-endian
(mips64, n64): the runtime byte-swaps little-endian reads on big-endian
hosts, and the compiler emits rodata (embedded constants) in the target's
endianness via --iree-vm-bytecode-rodata-big-endian.

Also fixes a few latent endianness bugs surfaced on big-endian
(vm.switch.i64, HAL fill patterns, packed ZIP header reads).

LE-only serialization features (HAL replay/profile files, FatELF writing)
return UNIMPLEMENTED on big-endian. Adds a QEMU CI job for mips64 and
documents the big-endian build in build_tools/cmake/README-mips.md.

Assisted-by: Claude (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Andrea Milosevic <andrea.milosevic@htecgroup.com>
name: pr-greeter

commit_message:
Add QEMU CI for the MIPS64 (mips64el) VMVX runtime

Adds a PkgCI job that cross-compiles the VMVX-only runtime for mips64el
and runs the runtime test suite under qemu-mips64el, reusing the prebuilt
host packages. The cross toolchain and QEMU come from the Ubuntu archive.
Mirrors the existing RISC-V 64 QEMU job.

Assisted-by: Claude (Anthropic)
Signed-off-by: Andrea Milosevic <andrea.milosevic@htecgroup.com>
